W
ith hym ther was his sone / aȝong squier
A louier a lusty bacheler
Wit lokkes crulle / as they were leyde in presse
Of xxᵗⁱ . ȝere of age / was he as I gesse
Of his stature / he was of Euene lengthe
And wonderly deliuer / and greet of strengthe
And he had ben somtyme / in Chiuachie
In Flaundres in Artoys / and in Picardie
And born hym wel / as of so litel space
In hope to stonden / in his lady grace
Enbrowded was he / as it were a mede
All ful of fresshe / floures white and rede
Syngynge he was . / or flowtynge al the day
He was as fressh / as is the monthe of May
Short was his gowne / with sleues longe and wyde
Wel cowde he sitte on hors / and fayre ryde
He cowde songes make / and wel endite
Iuste and eek daunce / and wel portreye and write
So hote he loued / that by nyghter tale
He slepte no more / than doth a nyghtyngale
Curteys he was / lowely and seruisable
And carf bifore / his fader atte table
A
yeman hadde he / and seru

At that tyme / for hym lust ride so
And he was clad / in coote and hood of grene
A sheef of pecok arwes / brighte and kene
Vnder his belte / he bar ful thriftily
Wel cowde he dresse / his takel ȝomanly
His arwes drouped / nought with fotheres lowe
And in his hand / he bar a mighty bowe
A not heed had he / with a bro

visage
Of wode craft / wel cowde he al the vsage
Vp on his arme / he bar a gay bracer
And by his side / a swerd and a bokeler
And on that other side / a gay daggere
Harneysed wel / and sharp as poynt of spere
A xpofre on his brest / of siluer shene
An horn he bar / the bawdrik was of grene
A foster was he / sothely as I gesse.

her was also a Nonne a Prioresse
That of hir smilynge was ful symple and coy
Hir grettest othe was but by seint loy
And she was cleped / madame Englentyne
Ful wel she song / the seruice diuyne
Entuned in hir nose ful semely
And frenssh she spak / ful faire and fetisly
After the Scole of Stratford atte Bowe
For frenssh of Parys / was to hir vnknowe
At mete wel y taught / was she with alle
She leet no morsel / fro hir lippes falle
Ne wette hir fyngres in hir sauce depe
Wel cowde she carie a morsel / and wel kepe
That no drope / ne fille vpon hir breste
In curtesie was sette / ful moche hir leste

That in hir cuppe / ther was no ferthing sene
Of grece whan she / dronken hadde hir draught
Ful semely after hir mete she raught
And sikerly she was of greet disport
And ful plesant / and amyable of port
And peyned hir to countrefete chere
Of court / and to ben estately of man

But for to speken of hir conscience
She was so charitable / and so pitous
She wolde wepe ȝif she sawe a mous
Kaught in a trappe / ȝif it were ded or bledde
Of smale houndes / hadde she that she fedde
With rosted flessh or mylk or wastel brede
But sore wepte she / ȝif eny of hem were dede
Or ȝif men smote it with a ȝerde smerte
And al was conscience / and tendernesse of herte
Ful semely hir wympel / pinched was
Hir nose was streight / hir eyen grey as glas
Hir mouth ful smal / and ther to softe and rede
But sikerly she hadde a faire forhede
It was almost a spane brode I towe
For hardely she was not vndergrowe
Ful fetys was hir cloke / as I was war
Of smal coral / a boute hir arm she bar
A peire of bedes / gauded al with grene
And ther on heeng / a broche of gold ful shene
On which ther was first / writen a crowned A
And after / Amor vincit omnia .
Another nonne / with hir had she
That was hir Chapeleyn / and prestes thre

Monk ther was / a fair for the maystrie
An out Rider / that loued venerie
A manly man / to ben an abbot able
Ful many a deynte hors / hadde he in stable
And whan he rood / men myghte his bridel here
Clinkynge in a whistelynge wynd as clere
And eek as lowde / as doth the chapel belle
There as this lord / was keper of the celle
The rewle of seint Maure / or of seint beneit
By cause that it was old / and somdel streit
This ilke monk / leet olde thinges pace
And heeld after the newe world the space
He ȝaf nought of the text / a pulled hen
That seith that hunters / be nouȝt holy men
Ne that a monk / whan he is recheles
Is likned til a fissh / that is waterles
This is to say a monk out of his cloystre
But thilke text / heeld he nought worth an oystre
And I seide his opinio

un
/ was right good
What shulde he studie / or make hym self wood
Vpon a book / in cloystre alwey to poure
Or swynke with his hondes / or laboure
As Austyn bit / how shal the world be serued
Lat austyn haue / his swynk to hym reserued
Therfore he was / a prikasour aright
Grehoundes he hadde / as swifte as foul in flight
Of prikyng and of huntyng for the hare
Was al his lust / for no cost wolde he spare
I seigh his sleues / y purfiled at the hond
With grys / and that the fynest of a lond
And for to festne his hood / vnder his chynne

And eek his face / as he hadde ben anoynt
He was a lord ful fat and in good poynt
His eyen stepe and / rolled in his hede
That stremed as a furneys of lede
His botes souple his hors in grete astate
Now certeinly he was a faire prelate
He nas not pale as a forpyned gost
